_comment: "text_gate": true opts a fixture into corpus/generated/text-diff.sh, which compares what InDesign's reference PRINTS (pdftotext) with the lines the engine lays out, page by page, as a character multiset; "lines" also compares the line breaks. Opt a fixture in once it passes; never opt one out to make a failure go away.
Per-fixture worst-page tolerances for the generated IDML/PDF corpus.
Each fixture's renderer-vs-pdftoppm output is gated on these numbers in
CI (.github/workflows/fidelity.yml -> corpus/generated/diff.sh).
Semantics: a fixture passes iff *every* page that has a matching
reference PDF page (cand-NNN.png + ref-NNN.png) satisfies
mean_de <= max_mean_de AND p99_de <= max_p99_de AND ssim >= min_ssim.
Pages without a matching reference are skipped (max_pages_with_pdf bounds
this — IDMLs that grew past their last InDesign-export are still allowed
to run; only the first N pages are gated).
Calibration: thresholds were originally sized to the worst observed page
+ ~15-25% headroom so noise does not flap. They are periodically
*tightened* (never loosened to mask a regression) so a fixture running
well below its budget actually catches future regressions.
Tightening rule of thumb:
worst_current / threshold ratio  →  action
> 75%                          →  leave alone (close to the edge)
50–75%                         →  drop to worst * 1.15 (15% headroom)
≤ 50%                          →  drop to worst * 1.20 (20% headroom)
SSIM is raised toward (worst_min - ~0.005) once there is ≥0.010 headroom.
Long-term goal stays the idea.md §13.2 budget:
mean ΔE <= 1.0, p99 ΔE <= 2.5, SSIM >= 0.99 (every page).
Tightening below those targets needs a (now generously achieved) measurement
to justify it; loosening any threshold needs a written rationale in the
commit message.

fixtures.name: gradient-geometry
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-12 (ADR 120, R-02a): where a linear gradient runs, asked of InDesign 20.0.1. Page 1: GradientFillAngle 0/45/90/135/180/-90 with no start or length on a square, a 2:1 rectangle and a square rotated 30 degrees; page 2: explicit GradientFillStart + Length, three-stop midpoints (default, 20 on stop 1, 80 on stop 2), a text frame fill, a gradient stroke, an inline anchored rectangle and two gradient feathers. InDesign turns the angle counter-clockwise on the page (axis (cos t, -sin t) in inner y-down coordinates, 90 degrees runs bottom to top), starts the default axis at the inner box's bottom-left corner with the box's WIDTH as its length (its own re-export writes GradientFillStart="0 h" GradientFillLength="w"), runs an explicit start in inner coordinates, and bends the segment BEFORE the stop that carries a Midpoint with N = ln 0.5 / ln m (3.10628 for 20 and 80). The engine drew 90 degrees top-down, ignored GradientFillStart on linear gradients and bent the segment after the stop: mean 7.789 / p99 82.338 / ssim 0.8768 (p1), 3.926 / 84.138 / 0.9390 (p2). After: 1.629 / 49.243 / 0.9748 (p1), 0.175 / 4.191 / 0.9970 (p2); sized at worst * 1.20 and ssim - 0.005. The residue on p1 is the rotated column alone (every unrotated case is within 1 RGB level on average): for a rotated frame with no start InDesign synthesises its default in page space (its re-export writes GradientFillStart="-7.32 12.68" GradientFillLength="109.28", the page bounding box's width, for an 80 pt square at 30 degrees) where the engine keeps the inner bottom-left / inner width. Real InDesign documents always carry an explicit start (91 of 91 gradient-filled items in the corpus packs). Case 28 (a gradient feather with no start) also differs: InDesign's undeclared feather default spans 69 pt over a 60 pt frame.

fixtures.name: tints
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-12 (ADR 120, R-03): how a tint of a CMYK colour prints, asked of InDesign 20.0.1. Page 1: process C, M, Y, [Black], a rich black and four brand colours x tint 100/80/60/40/20/5, each square at FillTint beside the <Tint> swatch of the same value; page 2: a StrokeTint, 48 pt text at FillTint, a gradient stop on a <Tint>, a CMYK-defined spot at FillTint and as <Tint> swatches, and a <Tint> at a FillTint. InDesign exports FillTint and the <Tint> swatch identically, as the base's inks scaled by the tint (`0.34 0.04 0.16 0 k` for teal 85/10/40/0 at 40, in fills, text, strokes and gradient stops; the spot as its Separation at the tint), so the page colour is the scaled ink through the CMYK profile. The reference is InDesign 2025's own export, and all 306 lines land where InDesign put them, within 0.12 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/span_columns_pipeline.rs). Worst page measured: mean 0.162 / p99 0.000 / ssim 0.9858; sized at worst * 1.20, the p99 at the 0.3 floor other fixtures use, ssim worst - 0.005. Body copy is Inter, registered by split-boundaries.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.129 / p99 0.000 / ssim 0.9874 (was 0.162 / 0.000 / 0.9858); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: tab-breaks
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign where a line breaks when a tab decides it (core: the composer measures each tab at the width it takes on its line, paged_text::layout::tab_aware_breaks). Page 1: fourteen cases with a tab near the right edge of a 200 pt frame (a left stop the next word no longer fits after, a stop the word after the tab cannot fit at, default and explicit stops exceeding the measure, right/decimal/center stops near the edge, a tab past the last explicit stop, a stop beyond the frame, justified text with a tab). Page 2: Left/Right/Center/Decimal minimum-width sweeps and edge probes. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; every asserted word sits on InDesign's line within 0.5 pt (pinned structurally by crates/paged-renderer/tests/tab_breaks_pipeline.rs). Before the change the pages measured mean 0.801 / p99 28.53 / ssim 0.9625 (page 1) and 0.476 / 14.53 / 0.9820 (page 2); after, worst page mean 0.403 / p99 13.177 / ssim 0.9842; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE, not the tab rule: c09's tab-free last line (InDesign sets its spaces at 70 %, below the 80 % minimum, to keep one word the engine wraps) and two edge probes InDesign keeps on the line by squeezing a 0.1 pt overflow. Frames carry no stroke: InDesign insets a frame's text by half a centre-aligned stroke. Body copy is Inter, registered by tab-breaks.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (stroke-inset: a text frame's stroke insets its text, and the gate draws glyphs at pdftoppm's sub-pixel phase): worst page now mean 0.176 / p99 3.202 / ssim 0.9942 (was 0.403 / 13.177 / 0.9842); re-sized by the rule above.

fixtures.name: stroke-inset
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign how a text frame's stroke moves its text. Thirty-one one-frame cases on two pages (Inter 10/12, LeadingOffset, hyphenation off; one-line paragraphs alternating left/right): stroke weights 0.25 / 1 / 6 / 12 pt at centre / inside / outside, a stroke with no colour, InsetSpacing plus a stroke, frames whose height lets the stroke decide whether the fifth line fits, two-column frames, rounded corners and a chamfered polygon. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; its rule (a painted stroke insets the text area on all four sides by half its weight centred, all of it inside, none outside, on top of InsetSpacing; the gutter is unchanged) is pinned line by line within 0.05 pt by crates/paged-renderer/tests/stroke_inset_pipeline.rs. Worst page measured: mean 4.025 / p99 84.138 / ssim 0.8960; sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (a text frame's StrokeAlignment reaches the model, plugin-publish 2ab572b, and the renderer strokes the outline it names): the twelve inside / outside frames, which were painted and inset as centred, now paint and set where InDesign does (pinned within 0.05 pt); worst page mean 4.025 -> 0.534, p99 84.138 -> 8.891, ssim 0.8960 -> 0.9724 (page 2), all <= 50% of the old budget, so sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE: the rounded-corner frames (the engine does not lay text out around corner effects); and shaped frames, which the engine does not inset by their stroke yet (see text_area_frame). Body copy is Inter, registered by stroke-inset.fonts.sh. TIGHTENED 2026-10-01 (shaped frames are inset by their stroke too, and the chamfered cases 27-30 land on InDesign's lines): worst page now mean 0.228 / p99 4.474 / ssim 0.9872 (was 0.534 / 8.893 / 0.9724); mean and p99 x1.20 (<=50%), ssim worst - 0.005.

fixtures.name: shaped-bands
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-01 to ask InDesign how lines fit SHAPED text frames. Eighteen frames on three pages (Inter 10/12, hyphenation off): a circle, an apex-up triangle, a square donut whose hole splits the middle rows, a chamfered rectangle, a rectangle with a notch (every edge on a whole point) and a narrow ellipse, set left / right / centred / justified, AscentOffset and LeadingOffset, with insets and painted strokes. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's own export; every line (text, ink start / end, baseline) is pinned within 0.05 pt by crates/paged-renderer/tests/shaped_bands_pipeline.rs. Worst page measured: mean 0.455 / p99 12.393 / ssim 0.9911 (the engine before the band rules: 5.848 / 84.138 / 0.7260); sized at worst * 1.20 and worst_ssim - 0.005. KNOWN RESIDUE: the justified donut (InDesign letterspaces a lone word across its part of a split row) and one line of the stroked circle (1 pt). Body copy is Inter, registered by shaped-bands.fonts.sh.

fixtures.name: blank-paragraphs
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-02 (RFI C-56): a paragraph with no word still takes a line. Six frames of A / something / B in Inter 10/12; the reference is InDesign 20.0.1's export. A paragraph of spaces is a line at its own leading (it laid out no line and took no room before); crates/paged-renderer/tests/blank_paragraphs_pipeline.rs pins all six distances, the truly empty paragraph as a named known difference (the IDML importer drops its range's leading, RFI C-57: 2.4 pt). fixtures.name: mixed-leading
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-02 (RFI C-59): a line takes the largest leading among its characters, and sits its OWN leading below the line before it. Six frames, Inter 10 pt, lines fixed by forced line breaks; the reference is InDesign 20.0.1's export. The engine gave every line the paragraph's first run's leading and stepped by the previous line's. crates/paged-renderer/tests/mixed_leading_pipeline.rs pins every step; one frame is a named known difference (the forced break ending a line counts for that line in InDesign). fixtures.name: hard-hyphen

One page, six texts at five frame widths, Inter 10/12; the reference is InDesign 20.0.1's export. 27 of 30 frames break exactly as InDesign's (crates/paged-renderer/tests/hard_hyphen_pipeline.rs pins all 30, the other three as named known differences that are not about the hyphen rule). fixtures.name: line-ends
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-03 (RFI C-62): a pen path's stroke end cap and line ends. One page, no text: open polygons in the three caps, with line ends (circle/triangle, barbed/simple-wide, square at 150 % + triangle at 50 %), a compound path of two open contours, a closed triangle with line ends set, graphic lines in round/projecting caps, and dashed ellipses in the three caps; the reference is InDesign 20.0.1's export. InDesign agrees on every cap, on line ends for EACH open contour of a compound path, and on none for a closed one. Measured mean 0.497 / p99 1.952 / ssim 0.9854 (the same IDML with the attributes the pre-C-62 reader ignored stripped: 0.710 / 8.739 / 0.981); sized at worst * 1.20 and ssim - 0.005. The residue is named, not C-62's: arrowhead geometry (InDesign trims the stroke under the head and draws Simple/SimpleWide/Barbed/hollow-Square differently) and the dash distribution on a closed path (InDesign spreads dashes evenly).

fixtures.name: line-shadows
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-06 (ADR 130): what casts an object's drop shadow when the object has no fill. One page, no text, every item with the same shadow (offset 6/6 pt, Size 4, black 75 %): graphic lines at 6 pt round caps, 1 pt butt caps and a 6 pt projecting-cap diagonal; a 6 pt round-capped open polygon (a pen path); a closed stroke-only triangle; a filled triangle with no stroke; a filled, stroked oval. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's export. InDesign casts the shadow from what the object paints: a line's and an unfilled polygon's from the stroke band including caps, a filled and stroked oval's from the ellipse plus the stroke's outer half. The engine matched the lines already (shadow profiles within 0.05 coverage); unfilled polygons cast nothing and the oval stamped its bounding rectangle: mean 0.382 / p99 13.140 / ssim 0.9864. With ovals and polygons stamping their painted outline: 0.051 / 1.879 / 0.9991; sized at worst * 1.20 and ssim - 0.005.

fixtures.name: rect-shadows
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-07 (ADR 130): what casts a rectangle's and a text frame's drop shadow. One page, every frame 120 x 80 pt with the same shadow (offset 6/6 pt, Size 4, black 75 %): stroke-only rectangles at 6 and 1 pt centred and 6 pt outside; filled (grey 40 %) rectangles with a 6 pt stroke centred, inside and outside; a filled, stroked and a stroke-only rounded rectangle (radius 16); a filled rectangle with no stroke; text frames holding Inter 48 pt 'Hi', stroke-only, filled and stroked, and neither. The reference is InDesign 20.0.1's export. InDesign casts the shadow from what the frame paints, as for ovals and polygons: the stroke band with no fill, the outline pushed out by the stroke's outer part with a fill, the rounded outline for rounded corners, and with no fill the text as well. The engine cast nothing for stroke-only frames, the fill rectangle for stroked ones, the bounding rectangle for rounded ones and no text shadow: mean 1.182 / p99 36.149 / ssim 0.9558. With frames stamping their painted outline and unfilled text frames shadowing their glyphs: 0.145 / 3.847 / 0.9972; sized at worst * 1.20 and ssim - 0.005. The residue: the engine's shadow falloff sits about 0.4 pt inside InDesign's on every shadow (the filled rectangle with no stroke included), and the rounded-corner and glyph outlines differ by a fraction of a point.

fixtures.name: table-cell-baseline
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-12 (Wave 1 R-06): where a table cell sets its first baseline, asked of InDesign 20.0.1. Page 1: a row per FirstBaselineOffset (Ascent, Cap, X, Leading, Embox, Fixed min 30, Ascent min 30, Cap min 30, Embox in Lora) x top inset {0, 6} x VerticalJustification {Top, Center}, written on the <Cell>, Open Sans / Lora 20 pt, and three em-box/ascent text frames below. Page 2 is the same table with the policy from a <CellStyle>: InDesign sets it identically, but plugin-publish's idml-import does not read a CellStyle's FirstBaselineOffset, so page 2 (mean 1.078) is not gated until that half lands. origin/main's engine (every cell on its ascent; em box = point size): page 1 mean 1.140 / p99 65.829 / SSIM 0.9532. With the cell's policy, the minimum as a floor and the em box at (cap height + 1 em) / 2: 0.147 / 2.961 / 0.9960, every cell within 0.05 pt of InDesign's DOM; sized at worst x 1.20 and SSIM - 0.005. The residue is glyph anti-aliasing.

fixtures.name: nested-styles
fixtures.rationale: Added 2026-10-12 (ADR 134, A-11): nested styles in InDesign's spelling (<Properties><AllNestedStyles>), asked of InDesign 20.0.1. Twenty frames: a tab, word, character, literal-character and sentence delimiter, each through and up to; a chain of three; a Repeat loop; a drop cap whose character style is the first nested style (Dropcap) and a style drop cap with none; a 15 pt red nested range with an underline style applied by hand inside it; a style that inherits its parent's list and one that cleared it (EmptyNestedStyles); a range's own list. origin/main's engine read no <AllNestedStyles> list and drew every paragraph in its body style: mean 0.566 / p99 24.615 / SSIM 0.9854. With the lists read, the ranges set by InDesign's rules, the nested style layered under the hand-applied one and the drop cap's paint following the cap: 0.197 / 4.933 / 0.9951; sized at worst x 1.20 and SSIM - 0.005. The frames carry no stroke on purpose (a hairline rasterises differently in the reference). The residue is glyph anti-aliasing.

After: 0.133 / 4.168 / 0.9982; sized at worst x 1.20 and SSIM - 0.005. Frames unstroked, as in nested-styles. TIGHTENED 2026-10-13 (exact leading and advances, ADR 138): worst page now mean 0.105 / p99 3.278 / ssim 0.9988 (thresholds were 0.16 / 5.0 / 0.9932); re-sized by the rule above.
